summary: Capcom's dragon-themed JRPG series, spanning SNES and PlayStation mainline entries, Dragon Quarter on PS2, handheld and legacy-console rereleases, the modern Breath of Fire IV PC restoration, and the short-lived Breath of Fire 6 online service.

entries.title: Breath of Fire

emulation.notes: Use accurate SNES emulation and preserve the original aspect ratio.

primary.version: North American SNES release via bsnes
primary.why: The original SNES version is the base release with full-screen 16-bit presentation; the GBA and Virtual Console/Switch Online routes are useful rereleases but do not add story content.
primary.how_to_play: Use a legally dumped SNES cartridge image in bsnes or Mesen with integer scaling, or Nintendo Switch Online if an official subscription route is preferred.

entries.remaster_caveats: No full HD remaster documented; modern official routes are emulated legacy releases.

entries.title: Breath of Fire II

emulation.notes: Use accurate SNES emulation and original aspect ratio.

primary.version: North American SNES release via bsnes
primary.why: Breath of Fire II is a direct SNES sequel with later GBA and Virtual Console/Switch Online rereleases; the SNES version via accurate emulation has the best display/audio capture ceiling.
primary.how_to_play: Use a legally dumped SNES cartridge image in bsnes or Mesen. Nintendo Switch Online is the easiest official modern route if subscription play is preferred.

entries.remaster_caveats: No full HD remaster documented; modern official routes are emulated legacy releases.

emulation.emulator: PPSSPP; DuckStation for the PS1 original
emulation.notes: Use PPSSPP internal-resolution scaling for the PSP route; use DuckStation only for original-version comparison.

primary.why: The PSP version was reprogrammed for the handheld's native 16:9 display and includes an expanded fishing minigame; PPSSPP provides the highest-fidelity capture route for that version.
primary.how_to_play: Use the PSP version in PPSSPP with high internal resolution. The original PlayStation version via DuckStation is the comparison route if you want the original 4:3 presentation.

entries.title: Breath of Fire IV

emulation.emulator: Native Windows; DuckStation for original PlayStation comparison
emulation.notes: Use the native GOG release for normal coverage; emulate PS1 only for comparison or if PC-specific behavior is undesirable.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Modern Windows PC rendering with integer scaling and anti-aliasing options.

primary.why: The modern GOG PC release includes Windows 10/11 compatibility, English and Japanese localizations, an improved DirectX renderer, integer scaling, anti-aliasing, restored environmental sounds, and improved input support.
primary.how_to_play: Play the GOG Windows release, configure integer scaling or anti-aliasing to taste, and keep the game updated because GOG has continued shipping hotfixes.

entries.remaster_caveats: The modern PC release is an enhanced preservation release, not a remake; keep it patched for hotfixes.

emulation.notes: Use high internal resolution and verify UI readability.

primary.why: Dragon Quarter is a PS2-only fifth entry that changes the series into a more experimental 3D RPG; PCSX2 is the highest-fidelity practical route.
primary.how_to_play: Use a legally dumped PS2 disc in PCSX2 with high internal resolution; test the Scenario Overlay/restart presentation before committing to a full stream.

entries.title: Breath of Fire 6

emulation.notes: Client/server availability is the limiting factor.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Windows/mobile service output while online.

primary.why: Breath of Fire 6 launched in Japan for Windows and Android before iOS followed, and official online operations ceased on September 27, 2017.
primary.how_to_play: Treat as a historical service-game entry unless a legal preserved client/server route exists; do not plan a normal playthrough.

entries.remaster_caveats: Official online operations ceased September 27, 2017; no offline edition documented.
